newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slip on U.S. Treasuries, calm mkt.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slip on U.S. Treasuries, calm mkt.

text.p: Argentine bonds slipped amid calm trade Thursday on the back of declines in U.S. Treasuries.
"The market fell because of the U.S., but there were no big sellers," said a trader at an Argentine bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell 0.15 to 117.70, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 declined 1/8 to 82-1/2.
"The market was very quiet," said another trader.

The market's biggest worry is the Tuesday meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting where it sets rates. Any hike in U.S. rates could knock U.S. Treasuries and in turn push Argentine bonds lower.
But traders began to say Thursday that even if the U.S. raises rates it may not be that critical to Argentina's market because of high global liquidity levels and improving economic fundamentals.

What is more, Congress approved the government's tax-hiking measures aimed at plugging the budget deficit Wednesday, ridding the market of an element of uncertainty that hung over it for nearly a month.
"If the Federal Reserve hikes rates and there is a market fall, I would see it as a good buying opportunity," said the first trader.

Next week could prove a difficult hurdle all the same because of the FOMC meeting first and then a 36-hour strike on Thursday by Argentine labor unions protesting the government's belt-tightening measures.
In the money markets, one-day call money rates fell to 6.28 percent from 6.45 percent.
